info.title: Nohead API
info.description:
The Nohead API manages projects, collections (your data models), their
fields, and records (your content), with full version history.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Servers, CI and agents use a
project API key (`sk_live_...`, created in the web app under API keys)
with scopes such as `records:read` or `schema:write`. Organization,
project, member and API key management need a person signed in to the
web app and are not available to API keys.

## Resources and IDs

Every object has an opaque, prefixed `id` (`col_`, `fld_`, `rec_`, ...)
and an `object` type. Record values live under `data`, keyed by each
field's `api_key`. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC. Deletes are soft and
can be undone.

## Lists

Lists return `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "next_cursor", "has_more" } }`.
Pass `limit` (1-100) and `cursor` to page, and `sort` (prefix `-` for
descending). Read on while `has_more` is true: a page can hold fewer
than `limit` items, even none. Records also take `filter[<api_key>]=value`,
`filter[status]` and `expand=<relation fields>`.

## Errors

Errors share one envelope: `{ "error": { "type", "message",
"request_id", "details" } }`. `details` lists field-level problems as
`{ "field", "code", "message" }`. Include the `request_id` when asking
for support.

## Safe retries and concurrent edits

Send `Idempotency-Key` on any `POST`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` to make retrying
it safe: the first result is stored for 24 hours and returned again for
the same request. Record responses carry the record's revision as an
`ETag`; send it back as `If-Match` to update only if nobody changed the
record in the meantime (`412` otherwise).

## History

Every change to a record is a revision, attributed to the person or API
key that made it: record revisions can be listed, diffed and reverted,
and collections keep a schema history. Send `Nohead-Change-Note` to
record why a change was made. Changes that rewrite existing values
(such as a field's type) are explicit, previewable field migrations.

How long revisions are kept depends on the organization's plan. Older
ones are removed, but every record keeps its first revision and its
last 10; `history_pruned_through` says how far history was removed.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Equality filters: `filter[status]=published`, `filter[deleted]=true`,
and `filter[<field api_key>]=value` for scalar field types (for
multiple-value fields: "contains value").

post.description: Creates a draft record (revision 1).

parameters.name: include_deleted
parameters.description: Also return the record if it is soft-deleted (to review it before restoring).

patch.description: Partial update. Keys present in `data` replace their values; `null` clears one.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the record. Values and history are retained; see restore.

put.description:
Publishes (`publish_at`) or unpublishes (`unpublish_at`) the record at
a future time (`records.publish`). The change is made within a minute of
the time, like a manual publish from the scheduler: it has its own
revision (`via: scheduler`), webhooks and audit event. `publish_at`
needs a draft; `unpublish_at` needs a published record or a
`publish_at` before it. Setting or cancelling a schedule is audited but
makes no revision.

get.description: The record's history, newest first. Available while the record is soft-deleted.

200.description: The revision with its snapshot and changes.

post.description:
Writes a new `revert` revision whose data is the target revision mapped
onto the current schema. With `dry_run=true`, returns a preview and
writes nothing.

200.description: The reverted record, or a preview for dry runs.
Changes from one revision to another.

post.summary: Redact a field from a record's history
post.description:
Removes every past value of a field from the record's revisions, for
example personal data or a secret that should never have been stored.
Each value the field had in earlier revisions (or only in the given
`revisions`), other than its current value, becomes
`{"$redacted": true}` wherever it appears in revision snapshots and changes;
copies in stored webhook payloads are replaced too. The current value
is never touched: to remove a live value, update the record first.

The only operation that rewrites history. It cannot be undone, needs
`confirm: true` (preview with `dry_run=true`), is audited as
`record.history_redacted`, and is limited to owners and admins with a
user session. Reverting to a redacted revision keeps the field's
current value.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Report what would be redacted without changing anything.

field.description: The field's API key, or its ID (`fld_...`, also for deleted fields).

revisions.description:
Redact only the values the field had in these revisions
(wherever they appear in history). Omit to redact every
past value.

confirm.description: Must be true to redact (not needed for a dry run).

200.description: What was (or, for a dry run, would be) redacted.

get.description: How many records match the filters, which work as in the list.

post.description:
Publishes, unpublishes, deletes, restores or updates
(`update` with `data`, applied to each) up to 100 records. Each record
is changed as if by its own request: one revision per effective
change, with its own audit event, webhook and search update. Records
that fail (not found, invalid, over a plan limit) are reported without
stopping the others. Publishing needs `records.publish`; the rest
`records.write`.

200.description: What happened to each record, in request order.

get.description: The project's collections. With `deleted=true`, those scheduled for deletion; published-only API keys get `403` for those.

post.description: Creates a collection, optionally with initial fields, as schema version 1.

200.description: The collection with its active fields.

patch.description: Changing the slug breaks clients that address the collection by slug.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the collection. Fields, records and history are retained and can be restored.

get.summary: Get the schema at a version
get.description: Published-only API keys read only the current version; earlier ones are `403`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Schema version; defaults to the current one.

200.description: The full schema definition at that version.

get.description: The collection's schema history, newest first. Published-only API keys get `403`.
Published-only API keys get `403`.

200.description: The schema change with before/after definitions.

get.description: The collection's fields. With `deleted=true`, its deleted fields; published-only API keys get `403` for those.

patch.description:
Changes that keep existing record values valid. After an `api_key`
change the old key keeps working for 6 months as an alias (see
`aliases`), so clients have time to move. Changing `type` or `multiple`, or a
`configuration` that existing active records would violate, is rejected
with `requires_migration`: use `POST /v1/fields/{field_id}/migrations`.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the field. Record values are retained and hidden until restored or purged.

delete.summary: Stop accepting a renamed field's old key
delete.description:
Removes an alias before it expires (`schema.write`): clients using the
old key stop working at once. Audited as `field.alias_removed`.

post.description:
Puts the collection's active fields in the given order (the order of
the record editor and of schema listings) as one schema change.
`field_ids` must list every active field exactly once.

200.description: The collection with its fields in the new order.

get.description: The collection's field migrations, newest first. Published-only API keys get `403`.

post.description:
Changes a field in a way that rewrites existing record values: its
`type`, `multiple`, a stricter `configuration`, or making it `required`
with a `backfill` for records that have no value.

Every record is checked first. With `dry_run=true` the result is a
preview: counts per outcome and sample records, nothing written. Without
it, a migration whose values do not all convert is refused (`422`)
unless `on_invalid` is `clear`; otherwise it is accepted (`202`) and
applied in the background. Poll `GET /v1/migrations/{migration_id}`.

While a migration is pending or running, writes to the collection's
records and schema return `409`. Each record whose data changes gets a
`migrate` revision, so cleared or converted values stay recoverable.

202.description: The migration was accepted and will be applied in the background.

get.description: Published-only API keys get `403`.

post.description:
A pending migration is cancelled at once. A running one stops at its
next batch and is rolled back entirely (`cancel_requested` is true until
then). Finished migrations cannot be cancelled (`409`).

get.description:
The project's assets, newest first. `deleted=true` lists deleted ones instead.
`content_type` lists only assets of those types, for example the ones an
asset field accepts (its `accepted_types`). Published-only API keys see
only assets that published records use, and get pages that can be short
(or empty) while `has_more` is true.

post.description:
Step 1 of uploading a file. Returns a pending asset and an `upload`: send
the file's bytes with `upload.method` to `upload.url`, with `upload.headers`,
before `upload.expires_at`. The bytes go directly to storage, not through
this API. Then call `POST /v1/assets/{asset_id}/complete`.

`content_type` and `byte_size` must be the file's; storage refuses another
content type and completion refuses another size.

The file counts toward the organization's storage from here on, while it
uploads too. On plans where storage is a hard limit (Free), a file that
would go over it is refused with `402 plan_limit_exceeded`; on others,
`Nohead-Usage-Warning` reports going over.

201.description: The pending asset and where to upload it.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the asset. The original is kept for 30 days, then purged;
records that reference it keep the ID.

post.description:
Step 2 of uploading a file: verifies the uploaded file (it exists, with the
declared size and content type), reads image dimensions and marks the asset
`ready`. Only ready assets can be used in records. Safe to retry: a ready
asset is returned unchanged. `422 upload_missing` means the file has not
been uploaded yet; `422 upload_mismatch` means it differed from what was
declared, and the asset is marked `failed`.

get.description:
A signed URL for a transformed rendition of a ready image asset
(JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP or AVIF). The same asset and options always give
the same URL, so it can be cached and embedded; it does not expire.
Only these options can be requested, so nobody can generate other
transformations. Without options it serves the original size.

parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: `contain` fits inside width × height; `cover` fills it, cropping; `fill` stretches to it.

get.description: A short-lived URL (15 minutes) that downloads the original file under its filename.

Full-text search in a collection, ranked by relevance (or `sort`).
With an API key, the collection must be `search_enabled` and the words
match its `searchable` fields only; members in the web app search any
collection, on all its text fields. Equality filters work on `status`
and on fields marked `filterable`; `sort` on `created_at`, `updated_at`,
`published_at` and fields marked `sortable` (`-` for descending).
Results are the current records; changes appear within seconds. At
most the first 1,000 hits can be paged through. `expand` embeds related
records and assets as in the records list. `409` when search is not
enabled for API keys, while a new collection's index is first built,
and when filtering or sorting on a field newly made `filterable` or
`sortable` until the rebuild that adds it has run (detail code
`rebuilding`; the index status is `stale` meanwhile).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to search for; empty matches everything.

get.description: Whether the collection's search index is built and up to date.

post.description:
Rebuilds the collection's index from its records in the background.
Search keeps working with the current index until the new one is ready.
Rarely needed: indexes follow record and schema changes automatically.

get.description:
One ranked list of matching records from the project's collections (or
those named in `collections`): with an API key, those with
`search_enabled`, matching their `searchable` fields as in a collection
search. `filter[status]` narrows by status.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to search for; empty matches everything.

parameters.name: collections
parameters.description: Comma-separated collection slugs or IDs to search in.

post.description:
Subscribes a URL to events. The response includes the endpoint's signing
`secret` (also after `rotate-secret`); verify deliveries with it (see the
`webhooks` section of this document).

201.description: The webhook, with its signing secret.

patch.description: Change the URL, description, event types, or turn it off (`enabled: false`).

delete.description: Pending deliveries to it fail at their next attempt.

post.description: The old secret stops working immediately.

200.description: The webhook, with its new secret.

post.description: Sends a `webhook.test` event to this webhook only. `409` if it is disabled.

get.description: The webhook's deliveries, newest first. Kept for 30 days.
The delivery with its payload and every attempt.

post.description: Attempts the delivery again now, whatever its status. `409` if the webhook was deleted.

200.description: A page of API keys. Tokens are never returned.

post.description: Returns the token exactly once. Store it securely. A project has at most 25 usable keys (`409` past that; revoke one first).

201.description: The created key, including its one-time token.

get.description: Projects in organizations the current user can read.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: List those scheduled for deletion instead (to restore them).

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: `filter[organization_id]=org_...` limits the list to one organization.

delete.description:
Schedules the project for deletion. It disappears at
once (its API keys stop working) and can be restored until
`purge_after`, 30 days later; then everything in it is permanently
purged. Confirm with the project's slug. Owners and admins.

200.description: The project, now scheduled for deletion.

post.description:
Cancels a scheduled deletion before `purge_after`, bringing the
project back as it was. Counts against the plan's project limit again (402).

get.description: Organizations the current user is a member of, with their role.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: List those scheduled for deletion instead (to restore them).

post.description: Creates an organization with the current user as its owner.

delete.description:
Schedules the organization for deletion with all its projects. It disappears at
once (its API keys stop working) and can be restored until
`purge_after`, 30 days later; then everything in it is permanently
purged. Confirm with the organization's slug. Owners only; refused (409) while a paid subscription is active.

200.description: The organization, now scheduled for deletion.

post.description:
Cancels a scheduled deletion before `purge_after`, bringing the
organization back as it was. Invitations revoked by the deletion stay revoked.

get.description:
Usage in the current period (the calendar month, UTC) against the plan.
Counters (`api_requests`, `search_requests`, ...) add up over the period,
with a daily breakdown; gauges (`records`, `asset_storage_bytes`, ...)
are current values. `api_requests` counts requests made with API keys.
The organization's members and their roles.

patch.description:
Requires `members.manage`. Only owners can grant the owner role or change an
owner's role, and the last owner cannot be demoted (`last_owner`).

delete.description:
Requires `members.manage`, except that every member may remove themselves
(leave). Only owners can remove an owner, and the last owner cannot leave
(`last_owner`). API keys in the organization's projects keep working.

get.description: Invitations not yet accepted, declined or revoked, including expired ones.

post.description:
Invites an email address with a role (`members.manage`; only owners can
invite owners). The invitee sees it after signing in with that verified
address and accepts it with `POST /v1/me/invitations/{invitation_id}/accept`,
and is emailed about it (see `email_delivery`). Invitations expire after
14 days. `409` if one is already pending for the address. Each
invitation is an email sent on your behalf, so they are limited per
inviting user and per organization (`429`), and revoking one does not
give it back. One address gets only a few invitation emails a day;
past that the invitation is still made, with `email_delivery.status`
`not_sent`.

get.summary: Review access left by former and demoted members
get.description:
What outlives a member's access (`members.manage`): usable API keys
whose creator left the organization, or whose scopes are beyond what
the creator's current role could grant, and pending invitations whose
inviter left or can no longer invite. Revoke them with
`DELETE /v1/api-keys/{api_key_id}` and
`DELETE /v1/invitations/{invitation_id}`.
Keys are never revoked automatically: they belong to projects, and
removing their creator must not break a deploy.

200.description: What to review; empty lists when nothing is left behind.

get.description: Pending, unexpired invitations addressed to the signed-in user's email.

post.description:
Joins the organization with the invited role (an existing member keeps
their role). Only the invited address can accept, by signing in with it
(`403` otherwise). `409` if the invitation is no longer pending.

get.description:
The plan, the Stripe subscription behind it (if any), and the plans on
offer with their prices. `enabled` is false until billing is set up on
the platform. Owners only.

post.summary: Start a checkout for a paid plan
post.description:
Returns a Stripe Checkout URL to send the owner to. The plan changes
once Stripe confirms the subscription; the owner comes back to
`return_path` in the web app with `billing=success` or
`billing=cancelled`. Organizations with a subscription change plans in
the billing portal instead (409).

Returns a Stripe customer portal URL, where owners change plan and
payment method, see invoices and cancel.

get.description:
Who changed what across the organization, newest first. Events hold
references (and a revision ID for record changes), never content. How far
back events go depends on the plan. Requires the `audit.read` permission
(admins and owners). `filter[project_id]` narrows to one project.

The project's audit events, newest first. API keys need the `audit:read`
scope and see their own project only.
Returns the service status. Does not require authentication.

The user or API key making the request. API key clients use it to
discover their project and scopes.

patch.description:
Sets the signed-in user's name, which their organizations' members
see. Sign-in asks only for an email, so a new user has none until
they set it. Session only.

delete.description:
Deletes the signed-in user's account, confirmed with the code
emailed by `POST /v1/me/deletion-code`. Their name and email are
removed, every session ends, and their memberships and the pending
invitations they sent are revoked. Changes they made stay in their
organizations' history, by "Deleted user". Organizations they are
the only member of are deleted with it (restorable for 30 days, as
with `DELETE /v1/organizations/{organization_id}`). API keys they
created belong to their projects and keep working; the access
review lists them. The same address can sign up again as a new
user.

Refused (409) while they are the only owner of an organization
with other members, or an organization only they belong to has a
paid subscription. A wrong or expired code is a 422. Wrong codes
count like wrong sign-in codes: after too many for the address, or
from the IP, every code is refused with 429 until the limit resets.
Session only.

200.description: The account is deleted, and the session cookie cleared.

post.summary: Email a code to delete my account
post.description:
Emails the signed-in user a six-digit code that confirms
`DELETE /v1/me`, valid for 10 minutes. Only the newest code works.
Refused (409) for the same reasons as the deletion, so the
organizations that still need the user are known before any code
is sent. Session only.

202.description: The code is on its way.

get.description:
Feature flags evaluated for the caller. Without credentials,
only public flags are returned, evaluated without actors (for the
marketing website). With a session or API key, client flags are
included, evaluated for the user and the given organization/project
(API keys: their own project). Server flags are never returned.

post.description:
Sent to each subscribed webhook when something happens in a project.
Delivery is at least once: the same event can arrive more than once, so
process events idempotently, keyed by `webhook-id`. Respond with any
2xx within 10 seconds; other responses and timeouts are retried 7
times over about a day.

Requests follow the Standard Webhooks specification
(https://www.standardwebhooks.com), so its libraries verify them:
`webhook-signature` is `v1,` followed by the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of
`{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}`, keyed with the base64-decoded
part of the webhook's `whsec_` secret. Reject requests whose timestamp
is more than five minutes away from your clock.

apiKey.description:
Project-scoped API key, e.g. `sk_live_k7fz0a9c3m2q_<secret>`. Used by
servers, CI, the CLI and coding agents.

session.name: nohead_session
session.description:
A person signed in to the web app: the httpOnly cookie its sign-in
sets, accepted only on requests from the web app's origin. Servers,
CI, the CLI and agents use an API key.

CollectionRef.name: collection_id
CollectionRef.description: Collection ID, or the collection slug when authenticating with an API key.

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description: Comma-separated relation or asset field API keys whose records or assets to embed under `expanded` (at most 5).

AuditEventFilter.name: filter
AuditEventFilter.description:
`action` matches exactly, or by prefix with a trailing `.*`
(`filter[action]=record.*`). `since` is inclusive and `until` exclusive.

Deleted.name: deleted
Deleted.description: List soft-deleted items instead of active ones.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The record revision you last read, e.g. `"7"`. Stale writes fail with 412.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
A unique value (1-255 printable ASCII characters) that makes retrying
this request safe. The first response (below 500) is stored for 24
hours per user or API key; retries with the same key and the same
request get it again with an `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header. The
same key with a different request is refused with `400`; a retry while
the first request is still running gets `409`.

NoheadClient.name: Nohead-Client
NoheadClient.description: First-party client identifier recorded in history (e.g. `cli/0.3.1`). Informational only.

ChangeNote.name: Nohead-Change-Note
ChangeNote.description: Optional reason for the change, shown in history (max 500 characters).

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window. Sent on every authenticated response.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RequestId.description: Unique identifier for the request, also echoed in error bodies.

ETag.description: The record's current revision, e.g. `"7"`. Send it back as `If-Match`.

UsageWarning.description:
Set when the organization is over a soft plan limit, as
`<metric>=<usage>/<limit>` (e.g. `api_requests=100234/100000`). Requests
still succeed. Any API-key request may carry it for `api_requests`.

ListMeta.description: Cursor pagination metadata returned with every list.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

has_more.description: Whether another page follows. A page can hold fewer than `limit` items, even none, while this is true.

role.description: The current user's role in the organization.

permissions.description: What the current user's role allows in the organization (empty without a membership). Clients use it to show only the actions that will succeed; the API enforces it either way.

grantable_scopes.description: API key scopes the current user may put on new keys: those whose permissions their role holds.

purge_after.description: When a scheduled deletion becomes permanent; null otherwise.

email_delivery.description: What became of the invitation email, or null while it has not been sent (or when sending is off). `sent`: accepted for delivery. `not_sent`: no email went out, because the address had bounced or been marked as spam before, or had already received several invitation emails that day. `bounced`: the email could not be delivered; check the address. `complained`: the invitee marked it as spam. Either way the invitation still works when the invitee signs in with the address.

name.description: Shown to the members of your organizations; `null` removes it.

purge_after.description: When a scheduled deletion becomes permanent; null otherwise.

id.description: Stable field ID. Never changes, even when the field is renamed.

api_key.description: Key used in record data. Part of the API contract.

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`). Not available for boolean, rich_text and json fields.

configuration.description:
Type-specific options, e.g. `max_length`, `options`, `target_collection_id`,
`accepted_types` (asset fields: MIME types or `type/*` wildcards that newly
written values must have; any file when absent), plus
the options for searches with API keys: `searchable` (the search words match the
field; default true for text, long_text, rich_text and enum), `filterable` and
`sortable` (default false).

aliases.description:
Old API keys of a renamed field that still work until `expires_at`:
record data also carries the value under them, and writes, filters,
sorts and `expand` accept them. Responses about the collection then
have `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers.

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`). Not available for boolean, rich_text and json fields.
A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`). Not available for boolean, rich_text and json fields.

search_enabled.description:
Whether API keys can search the collection (`GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}/search`).
Every collection is indexed; members can search it in the web app either way.

SchemaDefinition.description: The complete collection definition at one schema version.

id.description: The user (`usr_...`) or API key (`key_...`), or null for system changes.

name.description:
Resolved when read, never stored: a user's current name (or
email), "Deleted user" once they deleted their account, an API
key's name, or "System".

payload.description: Operation details, e.g. `changes` and `breaking` for updates.

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`). Not available for boolean, rich_text and json fields.

FieldMigrationRequest.description: The parts of the definition to change; omitted parts stay as they are.

configuration.description: The complete new configuration. When the type changes and this is omitted, only `description` carries over.

multiple.description: A list of distinct values (a repeated value is refused with `duplicate_value`). Not available for boolean, rich_text and json fields.

backfill.description: Value for active records that have no value, validated like a record value of the new definition.

on_invalid.description: `clear` removes values that cannot be converted (or backfills them); `fail` refuses the migration.

FieldMigrationCounts.description: Records by outcome, including soft-deleted records (which are converted but never backfilled).

conversion.description: `safe`: every value converts unchanged in meaning. `convertible`: every value converts, the representation changes. `conditional`: some values may not convert.

samples.description: Up to 10 affected records, invalid ones first.

before.description: The stored value before the migration, or null.

after.description: The value after the migration, or null when cleared or invalid.

backfill.description: `{"value": ...}` when missing values are filled in, otherwise null.

failure.description: Why the migration failed; null otherwise. A failed migration changed nothing.

RecordSchedule.description:
When the record publishes or unpublishes on its own (within a minute of
the time), set with `PUT /v1/records/{record_id}/schedule`. A time is
cleared once it has run. `last_error` explains the last scheduled change
that could not be made, until a new schedule is set.

RecordScheduleUpdate.description: A time in the future, or null for none. Omitted keys keep their value.

Via.description: The client a record change came through; `scheduler` for scheduled publishing.

ChangeVia.description: The client a schema change or field migration came through.

revision.description: Current revision number; also returned as the ETag.

history_pruned_through.description: Revisions up to this number (except revision 1) were removed by the plan's history retention.

expanded.description:
Only with `expand`: what each requested relation or asset field
points at, keyed by field API key: records for relation fields,
assets for asset fields. A single value is the object, or null when
it no longer exists; a multiple value is a list of those that still
exist. Expanded records are not expanded further.

Change.description:
One change between two states. Field changes carry `field` (current API
key) and the stable `field_id`; attribute changes (`status`,
`published_at`, `deleted`) carry `attribute`.

changed_fields.description: API keys of changed fields, and changed attributes.

redacted_fields.description:
API keys of fields whose values in this revision were redacted
(`POST /v1/records/{id}/redact`); those values read `{"$redacted": true}`.

revisions.description: Revision numbers whose snapshot or changes were (or would be) rewritten.

values.description: How many distinct past values were (or would be) redacted.

flags.description: Flag name to enabled, for every registered flag the caller may see.

user_id.description: The deleted user, as history still refers to it.

enabled.description: The collection's `search_enabled`; the index is kept up to date either way.

status.description: `building` until first built; `stale` from the change that queues a rebuild until it has run; `failed` if the last rebuild failed (it is retried).

event_types.description: The subscribed event types, or `["*"]` for all.

secret.description: The signing secret (`whsec_...`). Keep it private.

data.description: For `update`, the fields to set on every record (null clears one).

changed.description: False when the record was already in that state (no revision).

enabled.description: Whether checkout and the billing portal are available.

subscription.description: The Stripe subscription behind a paid plan, or null.

status.description: Stripe's subscription status; `past_due` keeps the plan while Stripe retries payment.

limits.description: The plan's limits; null values are unlimited.

prices.description: Empty for free and custom plans.

amount.description: In whole currency units, before tax.

return_path.description: A path in the web app to come back to, e.g. `/organizations/org_.../usage`.

reason.description:
`creator_left`: its creator is no longer a member.
`exceeds_creator_role`: it holds a scope the creator's current role cannot grant.

`inviter_left`: whoever sent it is no longer a member.
`inviter_cannot_invite`: their current role cannot invite to this role.

UsageRetention.description: How long the plan keeps record revisions (beyond each record's first and latest 10) and audit events, in days; null keeps everything.

grace.description: After a downgrade, the previous plan's longer retention still applies for 30 days; history past the plan's retention is removed after `ends_at`. Null otherwise.

revision_days.description: Days of revisions kept until `ends_at`; null keeps everything.

audit_days.description: Days of audit events kept until `ends_at`.

limit.description: The plan's limit, or null when unlimited or not limited.

enforcement.description: `hard` refuses changes over the limit (402), `soft` warns, `off` only meters.

daily.description: Counters only, one entry per day with usage.

project.description: The project the event belongs to, or null for organization-level events.

id.description: The resource's public ID (or key, for feature flags).

via.description: The client the change came through, when known.

metadata.description:
Small, action-specific references, e.g. `revision_id` and
`collection_id` for record events, `schema_change_id` for schema
events, `changed` attribute names for updates. Never content.

url.description: An https URL on the public internet.

id.description: The event ID, sent as `webhook-id`; the same on every attempt.

status.description: `pending` until an attempt gets a 2xx response; `failed` after 8 attempts over about a day.

response_body.description: The first 2 KB of the response.

WebhookEventPayload.description: The JSON body of every webhook request.

type.description: One of the event types, or `webhook.test`.

data.description:
`record.*`: `record` (the record after the change), `revision` and
`revision_id`. `asset.*`: `asset`. `schema.changed`: `collection` and
`schema_change`. `webhook.test`: `webhook`.

status.description: `pending` until the upload is completed; only `ready` assets can be used in records.

preview_url.description: A signed URL of a small rendition (fits in 640×640, WebP), for ready images; null otherwise.

byte_size.description: Exact size of the file in bytes (at most 100 MB by default).

headers.description: Headers to send with the upload.

ApiKeyScope.description: What a project API key may do. `webhooks:read` includes delivery payloads and `webhooks:write` can subscribe an endpoint to every event, so both give access to the record, schema and asset data in events, drafts included; published-only keys cannot have them.

token_hint.description: The non-secret start of the token, to recognize it.

PublishedOnly.description: The key sees published records only, for sites and apps: lists, reads, search and expanded relations leave out drafts and deleted records, and history is not available. Only read scopes (records:read, schema:read, assets:read, search:read) are allowed.

token.description: The secret token. Returned only once, at creation.

field.description: API key of the offending field or parameter, when applicable.

current_revision.description: The resource's current revision, for `revision_mismatch` details.

PlanLimitExceeded.description:
The change would exceed a hard limit of the organization's plan. The
detail names the metric (`field`) with its `usage` and `limit`.

Forbidden.description: The caller is not allowed to perform this action.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with current state.

PreconditionFailed.description:
The resource changed since the revision given in `If-Match`. Nothing was
written; `details` includes the current revision.

RateLimited.description:
Too many requests for this API key or user (or, with failing
credentials, this IP address). A published-only key is counted per
client IP, and all of an organization's keys together are limited too.
Wait `Retry-After` seconds; retries with the same `Idempotency-Key`
are safe.
